protocol_for_the_holder: 1. Eligibility: confirm in writing that you wrote neither the skill (fm-advantage-benchmark/) nor any replay case (fm-advantage-benchmark/cases/, astronomy/replay/cases/, astronomy/agent*/replay_cases.csv, astronomy/wave2/*/replay_cases.csv). Record name and date in the amendment ledger.
2. On receipt, recompute sha256 of both RULINGS_SEALED.csv files and of both cases.csv files; compare with this record. Any mismatch voids the corresponding seal; say so, do not repair.
3. Extract the polarity column from each cases.csv in the canonical form above and confirm its sha256 matches this record. Keep it with the rulings.

4. Take custody of holder_handover/id_map_*.csv (or regenerate your own ids and shuffle with a seed you draw), then have the coordinator remove from anything the stage under test can read: both RULINGS_SEALED.csv files, the polarity column of both cases.csv files, and the id maps. Record the commit at which that removal happened; any earlier commit readable by the evaluator voids the seal for the cases it exposes (REPLAY_PLAN 4.2 step 2).

5. Give the evaluator only SKILL.md, references/, and the blind cases file. The evaluator writes verdicts keyed by blind id in replay.py emit format (fired, ruling, via) and hashes the verdict file before any release.

6. Map blind ids back, join polarity, run replay.py score (or the patched split-polarity flow, patches/04) for development first, then sealed once. Report must-fire, must-not-fire and validator-only separately per module.

7. Write new sealed cases of your own that no panel agent has seen, per references/replay.md 'The limit that matters'; the existing cases were authored by the panel and cannot carry an independent seal.
8. Record the transfer in a new transfer_record.json with status COMPLETE, the holder identity, the hashes verified in step 2, and the removal commit from step 4.
